summary: Implemented all four J-series debt items (J2–J5) for WP-011.

J2 — MoviesListViewModel factory lambda: Replaced generic AddTransient<MoviesListViewModel>() with an explicit factory lambda in Program.cs resolving all 4 optional constructor parameters via GetRequiredService. Added 'using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;' to support ILogger<MoviesListViewModel>.

J3 — MostUsedThreshold cleanup: Removed the 4-line variable+discard block from TagsManager.PublishState; replaced with a single TODO (WP-J3) comment, eliminating dead code that would have been a CS0219 warning under TreatWarningsAsErrors.
J4 — Count-mismatch guard TODO: Converted the single-line return in DapperMovieCatalogRepository to a braced block with '// TODO: log Warning when ILogger is injected (WP-J4)' before the return.
J5 — CS8765 warnings: Verified 0 CS8765 warnings exist in TagsManagerTests.cs — criterion satisfied by current .NET 10 base class signatures.

constraints.md: Extended the DapperMovieCatalogRepository.GetMovieListAsync enrichment bullet in Tag Subsystem (M7) to note the count-mismatch guard carries a WP-J4 TODO and that ILogger injection is a future WP prerequisite.
Build: 0 warnings, 0 errors. Tests: 777 passed (255 unit + 335 App + 187 Infrastructure), 6 infrastructure tests self-skipped (no live DB).

comments.note: Program.cs: The MoviesListViewModel factory lambda uses GetRequiredService<T>() for all 4 optional constructor parameters. Since all are registered as singletons, this is correct — but removing any registration from DI will cause a runtime failure rather than a graceful null fallback. The optional-parameter design suggests nullable-safe degradation was intended; consider documenting in constraints.md if the degraded path is ever tested.

TagsManager.cs: MostUsedThreshold is configured but entirely unused at runtime (the TODO comment tracks this). When Most Used filtering is eventually activated, PublishState will need a Where() clause on allTags — no structural impediment.

DapperMovieCatalogRepository.cs: The count-mismatch guard silently returns an unenriched item with EffectiveTagWeight = 0. Without a logger, data integrity mismatches are invisible in production. Injecting ILogger<DapperMovieCatalogRepository> (WP-J4) should be prioritised before the next milestone.
